title: ALP per-NPU op-support table v1
description: One file per SUPPORT-TABLE IDENTITY, not per backend. A backend can publish more than one distinct table (Vela publishes exactly two TFLite tables -- Ethos-U85, and Ethos-U55/U65 -- invariant to --accelerator-config), so the file is keyed by (toolchain, toolchain_version, variant) under metadata/npu_ops/<backend_family>/<variant>@<toolchain>-<toolchain_version>.json, e.g. metadata/npu_ops/ethos_u/u85@vela-5.1.0.json. This is SCREENING data ('stance': 'screening'): it filters ops the compiler is documented/proven NOT to accept; it never certifies that a present op will actually compile (shape/quantization/graph-structure constraints this list can't express still apply). A backend with NO file under its directory is an intentional absence (e.g. metadata/npu_ops/ has no deepx/ directory -- dxcom publishes no op-support table) and MUST be treated by any consumer as 'undetermined', never as 'no ops supported'.

_generated.description: Present ONLY on authority=tool-generated tables: an AUTO-GENERATED / DO-NOT-EDIT banner naming the regenerating script. Absent on authority=vendor-manual tables, which are intentionally hand-transcribed (there is no tool to regenerate them from).

variant.description: Short table-identity slug. MUST equal the filename stem before '@' (e.g. 'u85', 'u55-u65', 'onnx-i8').

products.description: The NPU/product identifiers this table governs, e.g. ['ethos-u85'], ['ethos-u55', 'ethos-u65'], ['v2n', 'v2h'].

toolchain.description: Short toolchain name. MUST equal the filename segment between '@' and the trailing '-<toolchain_version>' (e.g. 'vela', 'translator').

toolchain_version.description: MUST equal the filename's trailing version segment (e.g. '5.1.0', '1.12').

precision.description: Optional: the quantization/precision this table's compile path assumes (e.g. 'int8'), when the toolchain has more than one and this table only speaks for one of them.

pins.description: Optional: other toolchain-internal version/config pins this table's accuracy depends on and that alp-sdk's adapter does not override (e.g. DRP-AI's {"drp_compiler_version": "100"}). A table is only valid evidence for a compile that used these same pins.

op_namespace.description: Vocabulary `supported_ops` is spelled in. MUST match the backend adapter's `accepts(src_format)` for this table's backend family: ethos_u -> tflite, drpai -> onnx. Comparing a model's ops against a list in the other vocabulary matches nothing and yields a categorically wrong no-fit verdict.

authority.description: 'tool-generated': produced by running the real compiler and parsing its own report (e.g. `vela --supported-ops-report`) -- reproducible by a scripts/gen_*.py script, never hand-edited. 'vendor-manual': transcribed from a vendor reference manual because the toolchain itself publishes no machine-readable report.

stance.description: This data SCREENS candidate ops; it never CERTIFIES a model will compile. An op present here can still fail to fuse/schedule on real hardware for reasons this list can't express (shape/quantization/graph-structure constraints); an op absent is a conservative negative, not a proof of unsupportability. There is currently exactly one stance value -- the enum exists so a future certifying data asset (e.g. a real bench-probed accept set) is a distinguishable, not-yet-invented kind, not a silent redefinition of this one.

source.description: The exact reproducing command (tool-generated, e.g. 'vela --supported-ops-report, table ... (column 1)') or the doc id + section + table name (vendor-manual). Never vendor prose -- a citation, not a copy.

tool_version.description: The compiler/translator version this table was read from, e.g. 'vela 5.1.0', 'DRP-AI Translator i8 v1.12'.

content_hash.description: '<algorithm>:<hex digest>' of the exact regenerated report (tool-generated) or the cited vendor document (vendor-manual), so drift in the upstream artifact is detectable without redistributing it.

note.description: Free-text grounding: invariance evidence, corrections made against a literal transcription (with justification), or caveats on what this table can/cannot certify.

count_expected.description: Optional self-check: the op count this table is expected to carry (e.g. from a vendor doc's own stated total). Cross-checked against len(supported_ops) by validate_metadata.py when present.

items.description: An operator identifier spelled in `op_namespace`'s vocabulary: TFLite builtins are UPPER_SNAKE (e.g. 'CONV_2D'); ONNX operators are CamelCase (e.g. 'Conv'). The pattern admits both -- it does not itself enforce which.
